title: Input Devices
subject: Computer Science
description: Keyboards, mice, scanners, barcode and QR readers, digital cameras, touch screens and microphones.
author: Erick

cards.back: The main and most common method of entering data into a computer, by pressing the keys on the device.
A keyboard created by software rather than being a hardware device. Also known as a virtual keyboard.
A keyboard where each key is programmed to do a specific task, with a picture overlay on it.
Under the keys is a grid of circuits (a key matrix). Pressing a key closes a switch, a chip in the keyboard works out which key it was, and sends that key's code to the computer.
Used to control a pointer or cursor on a screen, enabling a user to navigate around the screen.
The user rotates the ball while the main body stays still. It has buttons like a standard mouse and is more precise than a mouse.
Designed for people with limited hand/arm movement. It has two segments: one controls the cursor, the other is for clicking and selecting shortcuts.

cards.front: How does an optical mouse work?
cards.back: An LED lights up the surface underneath and a tiny camera takes hundreds of pictures a second. A chip compares the pictures to work out the direction and speed of movement, which is sent to the computer to move the pointer. The buttons and scroll wheel send their own signals.
Sensors detect how the ball is rotated, and this is converted into pointer movement on the screen.
Scans a physical document, e.g. a printed image or a text document, and converts it into a digital format that can be used on a computer.

cards.front: How are most scanned documents stored?
cards.back: As an image (but they can be stored in different formats, e.g. using OCR or OMR).
Optical character recognition: text on a scanned document is recognised and converted into digital text.
Optical mark recognition: scanned marks on a page are automatically converted to input.

The document is placed face down on the glass. A bright light moves across it, and the reflected light is directed by mirrors and a lens onto a CCD sensor. The CCD turns the light into electrical signals, which are converted into a digital image.

cards.front: How does OCR software recognise text?
cards.back: It compares the shapes in the scanned image with stored shapes of letters and numbers to work out each character, then turns them into editable digital text.

It shines light on the page and detects where marks are by how much light is reflected (dark marks reflect less). The position of each mark tells it which option was chosen, e.g. on a multiple-choice answer sheet.
Scans a 3D object using a laser or light source (or sometimes X-rays), measuring and inputting the object's geometry into a computer system.
The geometry of an object, measured and input into a computer system by a 3D scanner.

cards.front: What can a computer do with a 3D scan?
cards.back: Create a model of the object, either digitally or physically (using a 3D printer).
A device that recognises human physical characteristics, such as fingerprints. It also makes use of scanners.

cards.front: How does a fingerprint scanner work?
cards.back: It scans the pattern of ridges on the finger and compares it with fingerprint data stored earlier. If they match, the person is identified (e.g. the phone unlocks).
Numeric data represented as black vertical lines with white spaces in between.

cards.front: How does a barcode scanner work?
cards.back: It shines a light on the code and a sensor detects the reflected light. The signal from the light sensor is converted into numeric data.

cards.front: What is a barcode's number linked to?
cards.back: A database where further data is stored.
Item numbers for products in a shop (prices stored in a database), and order numbers in warehouses and distribution centres (customer details and delivery information stored in a database).

cards.front: What data can a QR code contain?
cards.back: Messages, URLs or telephone numbers. QR codes actually contain the data.

cards.front: How is a QR code read?
cards.back: It is scanned as an image and software decodes the pattern, e.g. with a QR code scanning app on a smartphone.
Encodes digital images and videos and stores them for viewing and later use, in its built-in memory or on an SD card.
The sensor a digital camera uses to capture an image.

cards.front: How does a digital camera work?
cards.back: Light enters through the lens and is focused onto the image sensor (e.g. a CCD). The sensor is made of millions of light-sensitive pixels that turn light into electrical signals. These are converted into digital data and saved as an image file on the memory card.

cards.front: How is a digital camera's quality measured?
cards.back: In pixels: the more pixels, the higher the quality of image that can be taken.
A mobile phone camera is normally about 3 or 4 megapixels, whereas a professional camera could be 28 megapixels.

An interactive device that combines a liquid crystal display (LCD) with touch-sensitive sensors. It recognises simple touches and gestures such as swipes, and a stylus can be used for precise control.

cards.front: Is a touch screen an input or an output device?
cards.back: Both: it is an input device and also an output device.
Uses the natural electrical signals in our bodies to detect when we touch the screen. It can't detect these signals through a glove.
Has multiple layers with space in between. When slight pressure is applied, the layers touch and the device recognises the touch.
A grid of horizontal and vertical infrared emitters and light sensors is arranged in front of the screen. The finger breaks the beam and the position is calculated.
An analogue device that records sound. The analogue sound wave must be converted into digital form (by an ADC) before the computer can process it.

cards.front: What can input from a microphone be used for?
cards.back: Speech-to-text software, in-game speech, and speech input for control.
Sound waves make a thin diaphragm vibrate. This creates a changing electric current that matches the sound (an analogue signal), which an ADC then converts into digital data.
